# A cyclic Selmer group generated by a point gives rank one

Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a number field $K$, let $p$ be a prime with $E(K)[p] = 0$, and let
$\delta \colon E(K)/pE(K) \to S^{(p)}(K, E)$ be the injection of the
[Selmer sequence](../cassels-tate-pairing/selmer-groups-of-abelian-varieties.md) (its item 2, for $A = E$ and $m = p$).
Let $y \in E(K)$ be a point of infinite order with $y \notin pE(K)$, and suppose that $S^{(p)}(K, E)$ is generated by
$\delta(y)$. Then $E(K)$ has rank $1$ and $\text{Ш}(K, E)[p] = 0$.

Proof (as Gross indicates, details worked out here): $S^{(p)}(K, E)$ is cyclic of order $p$, as $\delta(y) \ne 0$; as
$E(K)[p] = 0$ and $E(K)$ is finitely generated, $E(K)/pE(K)$ is an $\mathbb{F}_p$-vector space of dimension
$\operatorname{rank} E(K)$, which is at least $1$ as $y$ has infinite order; the injection $\delta$ then forces
$\operatorname{rank} E(K) = 1$ and $\delta$ onto, so that $\text{Ш}(K, E)[p] = 0$ by exactness.

## Depends on

- [Selmer groups and the torsion of the Shafarevich–Tate group of an abelian variety](../cassels-tate-pairing/selmer-groups-of-abelian-varieties.md), for $S^{(p)}(K, E)$, $\text{Ш}(K, E)$ and $\delta$

## Proof depends on

- [Selmer groups and the torsion of the Shafarevich–Tate group of an abelian variety](../cassels-tate-pairing/selmer-groups-of-abelian-varieties.md), for the exact sequence $0 \to E(K)/pE(K) \to S^{(p)}(K, E) \to \text{Ш}(K, E)[p] \to 0$ (its item 2)

## Sources

- B. H. Gross, *Kolyvagin's work on modular elliptic curves*, in *L-functions and arithmetic* (Durham, 1989),
  London Math. Soc. Lecture Note Ser. 153, Cambridge Univ. Press, 1991, 235–256: §2, pp. 237–238: (2.2), the sentence after it ("By our hypothesis on $\mathbb{Q}(E_p)$, the group $E(K)$
  contains no $p$-torsion and the dimension of $E(K)/pE(K)$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ is equal to the rank of
  $E(K)$."), and "Proposition 2.1 is an immediate corollary of Proposition 2.3, using (2.2)."
- H. Darmon, *Rational points on modular elliptic curves*, CBMS Regional Conference Series in Mathematics 101,
  American Mathematical Society, 2004; author's version,
  <https://www.math.mcgill.ca/darmon/pub/Articles/Research/36.NSF-CBMS/chapter.pdf>, cited by the page numbers
